NIST SP 800-63B is the 2017 edition (3rd revision), now withdrawn and superseded by 800-63B-4; it is used as a stable public-domain text. Each question carries the answer-bearing sentence copied from the document (extracted by the production parser): a chunk is relevant iff it contains that sentence.

documents.name: nist-sp-800-63b
documents.title: NIST SP 800-63B Digital Identity Guidelines: Authentication and Lifecycle Management

documents.name: attention-is-all-you-need
documents.title: Attention Is All You Need (Vaswani et al., 2017, arXiv:1706.03762v7)

questions.question: What is the minimum length for a password that the user picks themselves?
questions.sentence: Verifiers SHALL require subscriber-chosen memorized secrets to be at least 8 characters in length.

questions.question: How many failed sign-in attempts in a row may an account allow?
questions.sentence: Unless otherwise specified in the description of a given authenticator, the verifier SHALL limit consecutive failed authentication attempts on a single account to no more than 100.

questions.question: Does the standard want people to change their passwords on a schedule?
questions.sentence: Verifiers SHOULD NOT require memorized secrets to be changed arbitrarily (e.g., periodically).

questions.question: How should passwords be stored by the service?
questions.sentence: Memorized secrets SHALL be salted and hashed using a suitable one-way key derivation function.

questions.question: What is the smallest salt size allowed?
questions.sentence: The salt SHALL be at least 32 bits in length and be chosen arbitrarily so as to minimize salt value collisions among stored hashes.

questions.question: How many PBKDF2 rounds are recommended at a minimum?
questions.sentence: Therefore, the iteration count SHOULD be as large as verification server performance will allow, typically at least 10,000 iterations.

questions.question: After how much idle time must a user at the highest assurance level authenticate again?
questions.sentence: Reauthentication of the subscriber SHALL be repeated following any period of inactivity lasting 15 minutes or longer.

questions.question: How long can an AAL1 session last before the person has to sign in again?
questions.sentence: At AAL1, reauthentication of the subscriber SHOULD be repeated at least once per 30 days during an extended usage session, regardless of user activity.

questions.question: Is it acceptable to send one-time codes by phone call or text message?
questions.sentence: Use of the PSTN for out-of-band verification is RESTRICTED as described in this section and in Section 5.2.10.

questions.question: Should the sign-in form let people paste their password?
questions.sentence: Verifiers SHOULD permit claimants to use "paste" functionality when entering a memorized secret.

questions.question: Should services force users to include symbols and uppercase letters in passwords?
questions.sentence: Verifiers SHOULD NOT impose other composition rules (e.g., requiring mixtures of different character types or prohibiting consecutively repeated characters) for memorized secrets.

questions.question: What flag must a session cookie carry so that it is only sent over encrypted connections?
questions.sentence: SHALL be tagged to be accessible only on secure (HTTPS) sessions.

questions.question: How much randomness must a code sent over a separate channel have at least?
questions.sentence: The verifier SHALL generate random authentication secrets with at least 20 bits of entropy using an approved random bit generator [SP 800-90Ar1].

questions.question: What delay must follow failed fingerprint or face attempts?
questions.sentence: Impose a delay of at least 30 seconds before the next attempt, increasing exponentially with each successive attempt

questions.question: What is the appendix's view of other protections compared with strict complexity requirements?
questions.sentence: Furthermore, other mitigations such as blacklists, secure hashed storage, and rate limiting are more effective at preventing modern brute-force attacks.

questions.question: How many identical layers make up the encoder?
questions.sentence: Encoder: The encoder is composed of a stack of N = 6 identical layers.

questions.question: How many attention heads does the base model use?
questions.sentence: In this work we employ h = 8 parallel attention layers, or heads.

questions.question: What is the size of the inner layer of the position-wise network?
questions.sentence: The dimensionality of input and output is dmodel = 512, and the inner-layer has dimensionality dff = 2048.

questions.question: Which kind of functions generate the position signal added to the embeddings?
questions.sentence: In this work, we use sine and cosine functions of different frequencies

questions.question: How big was the English-German training set?
questions.sentence: We trained on the standard WMT 2014 English-German dataset consisting of about 4.5 million sentence pairs.

questions.question: On what hardware were the models trained?
questions.sentence: We trained our models on one machine with 8 NVIDIA P100 GPUs.

questions.question: How long did training of the smaller models take?
questions.sentence: We trained the base models for a total of 100,000 steps or 12 hours.

questions.question: How many warm-up steps were used with the optimizer?
questions.sentence: We used warmup_steps = 4000.

questions.question: What translation quality score did the largest model reach on English to German?
questions.sentence: On the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task, the big transformer model (Transformer (big) in Table 2) outperforms the best previously reported models (including ensembles) by more than 2.0 BLEU, establishing a new state-of-the-art BLEU score of 28.4.

questions.question: How large a vocabulary was used for the parsing experiments with extra unlabeled data?
questions.sentence: We used a vocabulary of 16K tokens for the WSJ only setting and a vocabulary of 32K tokens for the semi-supervised setting.

questions.question: How are attention weights computed from queries and keys?
questions.sentence: We compute the dot products of the query with all keys, divide each by √dk, and apply a softmax function to obtain the weights on the values.

questions.question: What do the authors claim is new about their model in the conclusion?
questions.sentence: In this work, we presented the Transformer, the first sequence transduction model based entirely on attention, replacing the recurrent layers most commonly used in encoder-decoder architectures with multi-headed self-attention.

questions.question: How many sentences were in the bigger English-French training corpus?
questions.sentence: For English-French, we used the significantly larger WMT 2014 English-French dataset consisting of 36M sentences and split tokens into a 32000 word-piece vocabulary [38].
